# Li et al. preference model reduction: v2 source adaptation

This version implements the strategy-reduction and preference-learning framework in *Fast and Interpretable Mixed-Integer Linear Program Solving by Learning Model Reduction* (AAAI 2025). Sources: [arXiv v1, including the appendix](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.00307v1), [published AAAI PDF](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/34916/37071). The methodological pin is arXiv v1, December 31, 2024. The implementation identifier is `li2025_source_adapted_v2_permanent_bounds_residual_attention_final_optimizer_v5`.

**This is an explicitly adapted implementation, not verified author code.** The v1 local prototype's frozen attention models failed to learn meaningful strategy rankings, and its deletion of inactive continuous variable bounds was not verified as author behavior. V1 files, models and results remain in their separate directory. V2 preserves the strategy method while retaining original variable bounds and replacing the unstable local network. Neither repair is claimed to reproduce undocumented author settings. Official AAAI pages, the paper and appendix, Wanyuan Wang's publication list, and Jiajun Li's public repository listing did not yield an author implementation in the bounded search on October 9, 2026. This does not prove that no author code exists.

## Preserved method and declared adaptations

| Component | Paper locator | V2 behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Strategy | Eqs. (4)--(7) | Original active inequality rows and the complete assignment of every integer coordinate, extracted only from certified training solutions |
| Reduced model | Eqs. (5)--(7) | Retain the selected inequalities, permanent equalities, all original column bounds, and the complete integer assignment; solve a continuous LP |
| Pair labels | Eqs. (8)--(10) | Solve every training-cost/training-strategy pair, measure original-model violation and relative objective error, then calculate negative-log rewards |
| SetCover | Strategy Pruning; Appendix Algorithm 2 | An edge requires both relative violation and relative objective-error tolerances; greedy maximum uncovered coverage with stable strategy IDs |
| Tokens and scores | Eqs. (13)--(15) | Varying cost parameters plus full strategy indicators, with a declared residual attention architecture described below |
| Preference supervision | Eqs. (16)--(19) | Same adjacent pairs sorted by true reward, tie preference 0.5, BCE preference loss and reward-difference squared loss; both averaged over pairs |
| Candidate prediction | Eq. (20) | Predicted top-k retained strategies |
| Final candidate | Eq. (21) | Minimum original-model violation among decoded candidates; equal violations follow predicted-score order, without inspecting test objective values |

### Permanent original variable bounds

The paper's formal Eq. (6) keeps selected inequalities, while its appendix describes `lb` and `ub` separately from `A_ineq` and `b_ineq`. The available text does not establish whether the authors retain bounds as the reduced solver's domain. V2 permanently retains the supplied `col_lower` and `col_upper`, then fixes all integer coordinates to the selected strategy. This preserves the original variable domain and prevents the unbounded output directions caused by the v1 interpretation in these UC cases. It remains a disclosed domain adaptation until author behavior is verified.

The shared canonical strategy representation includes finite bound sides as inequality rows. An active bound may therefore appear both as a selected row and as a permanent column bound; this redundancy does not alter the feasible set. Other inactive linear inequality rows are dropped. All permanent equality rows are retained. Selected rows remain inequalities, unlike MLOPT's active-equality reduction. Every returned candidate is checked against all original rows, bounds and integrality requirements. No original-IP optimality certificate is claimed for a reduced-LP certificate.

A cached active-equality vertex is used only when finite primal/dual values, active-row feasibility, permanent-bound feasibility, scaled stationarity and nonnegative selected-inequality duals certify optimality for the actual reduced LP. The remaining stationarity and primal residuals must also give a box-domain dual objective-gap bound within the stated numerical tolerance. Any negative selected-inequality multiplier triggers an actual LP, even if small. Otherwise a fresh single-thread HiGHS LP is solved. Unbounded, infeasible or unfinished decodes fail; there is no original-model repair or Full fallback. The candidates share one total 30-second prediction budget; a prediction returned after the wall deadline is rejected even if an earlier candidate was feasible.

### Residual attention adaptation

The published Eqs. (13)--(15) specify scaled dot-product attention, its L-fold composition, and a final score mapping, but do not supply numeric depth, width or activation. They do not explicitly specify residual blocks, LayerNorm or token MLPs. V2 uses those components as a stability adaptation inspired by the [Transformer's residual attention and position-wise feed-forward blocks, Sections 3.1--3.3](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762v7) and [pre-normalized residual blocks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.04745). These sources support the architecture choice, not equivalence with the Li authors' architecture.

Each token concatenates the standardized six UC generator cost factors or eight knapsack category value factors with a binary indicator for every canonical active row and the complete integer assignment. A shared linear/GELU/LayerNorm input embedding maps it to width 128. Two single-head blocks each apply pre-normalized attention with a residual connection, followed by a pre-normalized per-token MLP with another residual connection. The MLP expands to width 256 and returns to 128. A shared LayerNorm/128-to-64/GELU/64-to-1 head predicts each strategy's scalar reward. No positional encoding or dropout is used; strategy IDs do not create an artificial ordering signal.

The original losses average over instances and sum the same M-1 adjacent pairs. V2 also divides both losses by M-1. This common factor preserves their relative weighting and unregularized minimizers for a fixed strategy bank; it changes optimization scale, including its interaction with AdamW and clipping. It is not described as the published loss normalization. Lambda1 and lambda2 are selected independently, since Eq. (19) does not impose a sum-to-one relation. Numerical reward floors remain explicit below.

## Training, validation and eligibility

The input protocol supplies exactly 120 frozen training costs and certified optimal solutions per Appendix C.3 case. Structural models and training seeds remain fixed. A seeded 96/24 split uses only the 96 fit optimizers to construct development strategies, pruning edges and rewards. Validation optimizers do not generate development strategies. The unchanged 24 validation costs select development hyperparameters after the training sanity gate. Final extraction, pruning and fitting use all 120 training cases, with the uniformly declared final optimizer rule below. No test costs, solutions or objectives are read by this module. Fresh confirmation data are generated and evaluated only after configurations and models are frozen by the root runner; the old test results are not a tuning objective.

The fixed grid remains learning rate in {0.0001, 0.001}, lambda1 in {0.8, 0.9}, lambda2 in {0.1, 0.2}, and k in {1, 3, 5}: eight network fits and 24 validation configurations. All 18 cases now use 1,200 epochs, batch size 128, AdamW weight decay 0.01, gradient-norm clipping at 5, and learning-rate decay by 0.9 every 40 epochs. The paper's appendix gives AdamW, 100 epochs, batch size 128, decay by 0.9 every ten epochs, the same learning-rate range, and lambda1 in [0.8, 0.9]. Our optimizer settings, clipping, lambda2 grid, depth/width and residual architecture are disclosed adaptations.

This uniform optimizer update was chosen from a bounded training-only probe on the 96-fit-cost split of `uc_seed101_a0.5`, before any fresh confirmation costs were generated. With 96 rows and batch size 128, the earlier 300-epoch/every-ten-epoch schedule made only one gradient update per epoch. The probe compared that control with smaller batches and with 1,200 epochs/decay every 40 epochs; the latter used four times the integrated learning-rate budget and less fit time than the smaller-batch alternative. Its two tested loss-weight choices recovered 95 of 96 training optima but still had adjacent-pair accuracy below 0.55. These are training diagnostics, not test results or evidence that the full reward ranking converged. No reward, loss, strategy, hyperparameter grid, or held-out selection objective was changed. Attempt 3's frozen sources and failed reports retain the original settings and gate outcomes; they are not relabeled as successful fits or reused as attempt 4 checkpoints.

For each development fit and the final refit, the training-only sanity report records loss versus zero score differences and initialization, non-tie adjacent-pair ranking accuracy, score separation, top-1 reward regret, strict training recovery, cached Eq. (21) training recovery at the selected k, and the retained-pool strict recovery oracle. It also reports the best cost-independent strategy's strict and near-optimal recovery, reward regret, and the learned predictor's reward gain and number of distinct predictions. All recovery and cost-dependence quantities are diagnostics. A pool without a strict optimum, or one constant strategy that is optimal for every training cost, does not fail a recovery requirement; no such requirement is imposed.

For informative adjacent pairs, eligibility retains the original finite-output check, maximum within-instance score spread of at least 1e-4, and at least 1% loss improvement over both equal scores and the initialized network. Adjacent-pair accuracy and the unchanged 0.55 reference pass flag (`legacy_adjacent_gate_passed`) are recorded but no longer control eligibility. The paper specifies no such 0.55 gate; our training-only probe showed that this local criterion could reject a predictor that selected 95 of 96 training optima while misordering lower-ranked, nearly tied strategies. This readiness amendment is disclosed before fresh confirmation and applies uniformly to all cases. It makes no claim of full-ranking convergence. True differences up to 1e-6 are excluded from this diagnostic only; training still uses the paper's exact tie comparison. A single strategy or all tied rewards needs no ranking and remains explicitly marked degenerate. The remaining readiness checks are local safeguards, not author requirements or a generalization guarantee. A failed development trial is excluded before validation evaluation. If all fail, a failure report is saved and fitting stops. A failed final fit saves its diagnostic checkpoint but `solve` and the normal checkpoint loader reject it, preventing an unchecked model from entering the benchmark.

Among eligible development trials, selection maximizes strict original-optimal-value recovery on the 24 validation costs, then original feasibility, then minimizes relative objective gap, then k, then terminal development training loss. Strict value recovery uses the shared Appendix C.3 tolerance `1e-6 + 1e-9 * abs(v_Full)`. This development procedure, the paper's Eq. (21) candidate-selection rule, and the SetCover tolerances remain unchanged.

### Uniform final optimizer search, attempt 5

The same final optimizer rule applies to every case. With the selected lambda1, lambda2 and k, final fitting starts from the original seed on the all-120-cost strategy bank separately for each original learning rate, 0.0001 and 0.001. Both runs execute all 1,200 epochs with batch size 128 and decay by 0.9 every 40 epochs. Each epoch additionally evaluates the unchanged full training objective in deterministic eval mode after the optimizer update. The actual state with the lowest post-update objective is copied; a pre-update epoch loss is never substituted for the objective of a different state. Across the two retained states, the lower full-training objective selects the final optimizer, with original grid order resolving ties. A single-strategy bank has no ranking choice and retains its initialized state without gradient steps.

The selected state then receives the unchanged rowwise CPU readiness checks. Readiness, strict recovery and constant-strategy diagnostics do not choose a learning rate, an epoch, or a weaker fallback state. If the objective-selected state fails, the final diagnostic checkpoint and report are retained and the model remains ineligible. Development's held-out-selected hyperparameters and the actual final optimizer are reported separately. **Final learning rate selection is now based on the final training objective, rather than solely on held-out selection.** This is an explicit optimizer adaptation, not verified author code or a new validation result. No loss, reward floor, architecture, strategy definition, seed, candidate grid or test protocol changes.

This amendment follows a bounded training-only probe of the unchanged all-120-cost `knapsack_seed101_a0.2` bank. The earlier selected learning rate 0.001 had learned on the 96-cost development bank, but its 120-cost terminal refit made a constant top-1 decision: 8 strict training recoveries versus a retained-bank oracle of 101. The exact control reproduced that failure. Its actual best post-update epoch was 149, with loss 0.864290 and 53 strict recoveries. The original grid value 0.0001 reached loss 0.582790 and 101 strict recoveries at epoch 1,200. Those figures diagnose optimization on training labels; they establish no confirmation recovery or speedup. The 46.89-second probe used no solver calls, fresh costs or official checkpoint writes. Its frozen report is `audit/remote-attempt4/probe-extracted/li-finalfit-probe-attempt4/probe-report.json`, SHA256 `92e71cd4821cc8b926908a603834df3fda686ea2c8d870dfb551651546c4f597`. Attempt 4's actual failed checkpoint, terminal histories and source pins remain unchanged; attempt 5 retrains all models under its new source version.

The extra optimizer work is fully counted: eight development network fits remain unchanged, and two final learning-rate fits replace one. `development_selection_seconds` includes the split, development bank/pair construction, eight fits and 24 held-out configurations. `final_bank_preparation_seconds` covers final bank and pair preparation. `final_optimizer_search_seconds` covers both final fits, all post-update evaluations and state copies, endpoint and retained-state CPU diagnostics, and objective selection. Each `final_optimizer_trials` entry records its actual `fit_seconds`, full pre-update and post-update histories, best epoch/objective, endpoint and retained CPU diagnostics, and component timings. `additional_learning_rate_trial_wall_seconds` plus the declared checkpoint stages for the development-selected learning rate measures added protocol stages; it is not a causal runtime comparison with an unexecuted old run. Overall runner fit time remains the total cost.

`selected_hyperparameters` and `development_selected_hyperparameters` preserve the held-out result. `actual_final_optimizer` and `final_selected_lr` identify the optimizer used by the saved state. `selected_state_loss` is recomputed from that restored state on CPU. The complete `history` still ends at the true terminal state of the selected LR, which may be later than the retained best epoch; its last entry is not rewritten or described as the retained-state loss. The best state minimizes the full-batch objective on the fitting backend, without claiming it minimizes every epoch's rowwise CPU readiness statistic.

The fixed 120-cost budget does not run adaptive Good--Turing exploration to its stopping criterion. The singleton estimate is reported, without claiming the paper's coverage stopping guarantee. Additional pair-label LP solves are counted as offline work. Native Li always fixes the complete integer assignment. It has no target-K parameter: this row must not be presented as a matched-dimension variant. Any strategy-neighborhood modification would be a separately named algorithm, not implemented here.

## Numerical and solver conventions

- Eq. (8)'s unspecified denominator norm is the infinity norm of the finite canonical RHS, including equality RHS, with a 1e-12 floor. Eq. (9)'s objective denominator is floored at 1e-12 for zero-objective instances.
- SetCover uses relative violation and relative objective-error thresholds of 1e-4, matching the paper's reported accuracy tolerances. Final original feasibility uses the shared absolute 1e-6 threshold.
- Eq. (10) needs a convention for an exactly correct pair: the log argument is floored at 1e-10. Failed decodes receive penalty 1e6 and never form coverage edges. Successful finite penalties are not clipped.
- Exact reward ties receive preference label 0.5. Equal SetCover counts and predicted-score ties preserve stable strategy order. Eq. (21) violation ties preserve predicted-score order.
- Extraction active tolerance is 1e-7, rank tolerance 1e-10 and primal/bound tolerance 1e-6. Dual signs must be nonnegative without a negative tolerance. Stationarity must be at most `1e-9 * max(1, norm(c_continuous, infinity))`; its box-domain gap bound must be at most `1e-7 + 1e-10 * abs(candidate_objective)`. This is a numerical reduced-LP certificate, not an exact arithmetic or original-IP certificate.
- Torch training uses float32, deterministic seeds and either CPU or CUDA as explicitly configured. Decoding and original-model checks use float64. Inference for the comparison runs on CPU; Torch, BLAS and HiGHS use one thread. CUDA training sets `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` before importing Torch.

## Portable API and verification state

`PreferenceConfig(device='cpu', 'cuda' or 'auto')` controls fitting only. The default is CPU; the remote run must explicitly request CUDA or resolve auto to CUDA, and records both requested and actual devices. `fit_case(case, output_dir, config)` returns a fitted `PreferenceBaseline`; `solve(cost, features, total_time_limit=30)` returns candidate, original feasibility, elapsed time and individual reduced-LP diagnostics. GPU fits are transferred to CPU before validation prediction, saving and final inference. `load_fitted(case, output_dir)` rebuilds offline strategy factors without fitting, maps weights to CPU, checks the implementation version, training arrays, original model, strategy signatures and dependency source pins, and rejects a failed sanity gate. Runner eligibility is exposed as `metadata['sanity_gate']['passed']`.

Reports preserve the fixed grid, split indices, every trial's sanity status, epoch-zero and subsequent losses, gradient norms, selected validation configuration, training-only oracle diagnostics, pair-solve counts, cached versus new work, runtime and declared adaptations. Pair caches require exact source, configuration, original canonical model and training hashes. No test field is required by the fitting API. Model restoration occurs before serial CPU timing; fitting time and remote cost are reported separately by the runner.

Preparation checks passed: Python compilation; independent tie/pair-mean loss arithmetic; a 32-input/four-strategy synthetic learning problem (100 steps, loss 6.0836 to 0.09864, top-1 accuracy 100%); an inactive-bound changed-cost LP; a tiny-negative-dual/large-bound fallback example; and a 12-input/two-strategy synthetic end-to-end fit, checkpoint CPU restoration and zero-budget rejection. A deliberately delayed prediction was rejected, a corrupted pair archive was recomputed and then resumed correctly, and a zero-epoch fit failed the training gate. No real benchmark-case or test data were used by these checks. The synthetic fit passed the gate with non-tie accuracy 100%, 44.9% loss improvement and 12/12 training recovery. These establish interface and learning capability only. Full training and fresh-test numerical comparison are pending; no v2 recovery or speedup claim is made by this note.
